title: Gaussian mass of a cone
statement: Let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^2$ and $\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R$ be measurable. Suppose that for every $r>0$ and every $\theta\in\mathbb R$, $(r\cos\theta,r\sin\theta)\in A$ if and only if $\theta\in\Theta$. Then the integral of the planar standard Gaussian density over $A$, interpreted as a nonnegative extended real integral, is $(2\pi)^{-1}$ times the Lebesgue measure of $\Theta\cap(-\pi,\pi)$: $\int_A d_2(x,y)\,d(x,y)=(2\pi)^{-1}\,\operatorname{Leb}(\Theta\cap(-\pi,\pi))$.
hypotheses_covered: For every $r>0$ and $\theta\in\mathbb R$, $(r\cos\theta,r\sin\theta)\in A$ exactly when $\theta\in\Theta$
replaced: Let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^2$ and $\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R$ be measurable sets such that for all real $r>0$ and $\theta$, $(r\cos\theta,r\sin\theta)\in A$ if and only if $\theta\in\Theta$. Then $\int_A(2\pi)^{-1}e^{-(x^2+y^2)/2}\,dx\,dy=(2\pi)^{-1}\operatorname{Leb}(\Theta\cap(-\pi,\pi))$, with the integral and angular Lebesgue measure in the nonnegative extended reals.
